children: Shares of Hindalco Industries were trading at ₹958 on the National Stock Exchange around midday on Wednesday, down marginally by 0.21 per cent from Tuesday’s close of ₹960. The stock opened at ₹946.05, touched an intraday high of ₹965.25 and a low of ₹946, with over 64.80 lakh shares changing hands worth ₹619.85 crore by 12.45 PM. Sell-side orders outweighed buy orders, with 57.44 per cent of the order book on the sell side.

The stock has been in focus this week following its second-quarter results for FY27, reported last Friday. The company sits well below its 52-week high of ₹1,176, hit in May 2026, though it has gained over 20 per cent in the past year against a Nifty 50 that is down 1.59 per cent over the same period.

Brokerages remain broadly bullish on the stock. UBS maintained a Buy with the highest target price on the Street at ₹1,325, noting that Q2FY27 EBITDA beat both its own and consensus estimates. The Swiss bank flagged strong aluminium realizations and Novelis performance as key drivers. Motilal Oswal reiterated Buy with a target of ₹1,180, citing strong premiums, domestic product mix and copper byproduct gains. Axis Direct kept its Buy intact but trimmed its target to ₹1,060 from ₹1,155, reflecting softer aluminium realization assumptions for FY28. Nomura also held a Buy at ₹1,100, flagging that the third quarter is likely to be the softest before a recovery in Q4FY27.

On results, Hindalco’s consolidated net sales for the September quarter came in at ₹917 billion, up 39 per cent year-on-year. EBITDA rose 43 per cent year-on-year to ₹128 billion, though it was down 8 per cent sequentially due to higher coal and calcined petroleum coke costs. Adjusted profit after tax stood at ₹73 billion, up 50 per cent year-on-year.

Deliverable volume stood at 60.87 per cent of total traded quantity, suggesting a reasonable share of trades were backed by actual delivery intent. The stock’s current P/E stands at 11.24 times on a trailing basis.

title: Hindalco trades near ₹958 as analysts back stock post Q2 beat
